Subject: Mutual Action Plan draft + pricing ask — Nimbus AI

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the overview of Nimbus AI's inference ramp and the use cases for retrieval-augmented generation across your analytics product. I promised to send a short post-call recap and a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (attached).

High-level MAP (draft):
- Target close date: 2027-03-19 (customer procurement signed)
- Milestones & owners:
  1) POC kickoff — 2027-02-21 — Owner: Nimbus AI (provide test dataset & API access)
  2) Security & SOC 2 questionnaire complete — 2027-02-28 — Owner: Nimbus AI (answer questionnaire), Redwood (provide evidence + secure onboarding)
  3) Performance validation / latency SLA evaluation — 2027-03-07 — Owner: Redwood (POC run)
  4) Contract & procurement signoff — 2027-03-19 — Owner: Nimbus AI (procurement), Redwood (finalize T&Cs)
  5) Production enablement / go-live window — 2027-04-04 — Owner: Joint

Dependencies and blockers:
- Nimbus to provide anonymized sample dataset & IP allowlist for connectivity by 2027-02-18
- Security questionnaire needs a Red Team contact (we can loop infra)
- Procurement requires a committed spend; they indicated wanting clarity on price/credits and a one-year commit.

Pricing ask (what we discussed on the call):
- Proposed commit: $150k annual committed spend (platform usage)
- Customer request: 20% concession (either credits or discount) for year 1 in exchange for the commit
- Attached: pricing_summary.pdf with tiered unit economics and contract_term_sheet_v1.docx

Next steps (for Nimbus): please confirm the MAP milestones and let me know if the target close date still works.

Karthik — looping you to align on the scope for the POC and to confirm the resource plan.

Attachments: [Attachment: NimbusAI_MAP_v1.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 56 KB)], [Attachment: pricing_summary.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)]

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful and captures what we talked about. A couple quick clarifications:
1) Security timeline — our InfoSec team needs the questionnaire returned by 2/24 to make the 2/28 internal review. Will that timeline work for Redwood to provide the evidence URLs?
2) Commit level — the $150k works as a starting point for our procurement team; the decision hinges on the concession structure (credits vs discount).

If you can show a simple alternative (e.g., $30k onboarding credit vs 20% off first-year consumption) that would speed our internal approval. We'll prioritize the POC dataset this week.

Subject: Fwd: Mutual Action Plan draft + pricing ask — Nimbus AI — pricing/credit approval needed

Hi Nikhil / Vanessa,

Forwarding the thread with Nimbus — they're verbally aligned on a $150k annual commit but have asked for a 20% concession on year-one economics. Two options they asked us to price:
- Option A: $30k onboarding credit applied to first invoice (one-time)
- Option B: 20% off first-year consumption across the committed tier

Why this matters: closing at the 3/19 target keeps them on our Q1 ramp plan for the region and unlocks a multi-product reference case.

Attached: pricing_summary.pdf and contract_term_sheet_v1.docx with the basic commitment language.

Ask: can you review and confirm whether we can approve Option A or Option B? If approved, I need an executive sign-off (simple email) by 2027-02-12 EOD to keep procurement momentum. If not, please suggest counter concession (e.g., smaller credit + success milestone).

Quick background for context: deal HS-209384 (Nimbus AI) — POC scope is retrieval-heavy, expected QPS in pilot ~200 req/s, projected production ~$12K/month baseline if they convert.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T12:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Mutual Action Plan draft + pricing ask — Nimbus AI — pricing/credit approval needed

Marissa — thanks for the notes. I can approve a concession but would prefer it be structured as a one-time onboarding credit rather than an across-the-board first-year discount. Proposed approach:
- Approve Option A: $25k onboarding credit applied to first invoice
- Require commitment: $150k ARR (12-month)
- Add a milestone: $10k of the credit is contingent on production usage > 50% of committed monthly run-rate within 90 days of go-live (to align incentives)

Two asks before final sign-off: finance needs to review the term sheet for accounting treatment, and legal needs to confirm no long-term preferential pricing clauses that would block later discounts. If finance says yes, I approve the $25k credit with the contingency above.

—Nikhil
VP, Revenue Operations
